Document the PCR sample preparation protocol for the genomics lab. The steps must be followed in this exact order:
1. Thaw reagents on ice for 15 minutes
2. Vortex and centrifuge all reagents briefly
3. Prepare master mix: combine water, buffer, dNTPs, primers, and polymerase
4. Aliquot 18 µL master mix into each PCR tube
5. Add 2 µL template DNA to each tube
6. Seal tubes and centrifuge at 1000g for 30 seconds
7. Load into thermal cycler and run program: 98°C 30s, 30 cycles of 98°C 10s/60°C 20s/72°C 30s, final 72°C 5min
8. Hold at 4°C until retrieval
9. Run 2% agarose gel electrophoresis to verify amplification
10. Document results in LIMS with sample IDs and band sizes

5. Create combined PEM: cat portal.crt ca-bundle.crt > portal-fullchain.pem

8. Schedule production deployment during low-traffic window

1. Update all packages with apt update && apt upgrade -y
2. Configure UFW to allow only SSH (port 22), HTTP (80), HTTPS (443)
3. Disable root SSH login by setting PermitRootLogin no in sshd_config

14. USER enzyme digestion to remove second-strand cDNA
15. PCR enrich 12 cycles with indexed primers, purify 1.0x AMPure XP
16. Validate library size distribution and concentration on Bioanalyzer
17. Pool equimolar libraries and sequence on NovaSeq 6000 2x150bp

Create the incident response runbook for database primary failover. Follow this exact sequence:
1. Receive PagerDuty alert for 'Database Primary Unreachable'
2. Confirm primary unreachable: pg_isready -h primary.db.internal -p 5432 (expect non-zero exit)
3. Check replica lag: SELECT pg_last_wal_receive_lsn(), pg_last_wal_replay_lsn() on replica
4. If lag > 100MB, escalate to DBA on-call immediately
5. Promote replica: pg_ctl promote -D /var/lib/postgresql/data
6. Verify promotion: pg_isready -h replica.db.internal -p 5432 (expect 0)
7. Update Route53 CNAME record 'primary.db.internal' to point to replica IP
8. Wait for DNS TTL expiry (300 seconds)
9. Verify application connectivity: psql -h primary.db.internal -U app -c 'SELECT 1'
10. Run application smoke tests against new primary
11. Configure old primary as new replica when recovered
12. Post incident summary to #incidents channel with timeline
13. Schedule postmortem within 48 hours

Document the PostgreSQL major version upgrade procedure using pg_upgrade. Steps must be in this order:
1. Install new PostgreSQL version packages alongside current version
2. Initialize new cluster with initdb --locale=en_US.UTF-8
3. Run pg_upgrade --check to verify compatibility
4. Stop application connections to database
5. Stop old PostgreSQL service
6. Run pg_upgrade with --link flag for in-place upgrade
7. Start new PostgreSQL service
8. Run vacuumdb --all --analyze-in-stages
9. Update connection pooling (PgBouncer) to new port
10. Restore application connections
11. Run application smoke tests
12. Remove old PostgreSQL packages after 48-hour observation
